tech.name: Coding-agent session
tech.one_line: One AI model working in a loop with tools: it reads files, edits code, runs commands and checks the result, in your terminal or editor, until the job is done.

predecessor.name: Chat assistant (and autocomplete): you copy code back and forth

hook.text: You would never fix your car with the mechanic on the phone, but that is how you code with an AI chatbot. A coding-agent session fixes that.

claims.text: Chat-based assistants only respond with text you must apply yourself.

before.text: A chat assistant is the mechanic on the phone: it can only talk, so you paste its fix, run it, and carry the error back.

claims.text: Without tools, the model can only respond with text.
Agentic coding is defined as opposed to chat-based assistants that only respond with text you must apply yourself.

new.text: A coding agent is the mechanic in your garage, with tools. You give it one job in your terminal or editor; it reads files, edits code, runs a command and checks the result, and goes around again until done. The whole visit, every step and result, is one session.

claims.text: The agentic loop: gather context, take action, verify results, repeat until done; tools read code, edit files, run commands.
Claude Code runs in the terminal, IDE extensions, desktop and web; the loop is the same everywhere.
A session is a conversation tied to your directory; each message, tool use and result is written to its transcript.
Codex CLI: inspect files, make edits, run tools in one focused loop, in your terminal.
Copilot agent mode reads files, edits, runs terminal commands and tests, and auto-corrects in a loop until the task is completed.

why.text: You stop being the messenger. You watch, and you can stop it at any moment.

claims.text: The AI reads files, runs commands and makes changes while you watch, redirect, or step away.
You can interrupt the loop at any point to steer it.

takeaway.text: It can still be wrong, so give it a test to run. The model did not get a bigger brain: it got tools (hands) and a way to check its own work.

claims.text: The agentic loop is powered by models that reason and tools that act; the harness provides the tools.
Verification loop: give it a check it can run so it iterates until the check passes.

outro.text: Spoken call to action: subscribe for the next one. On screen: a Subscribe button and 'Next in 60 seconds: what are Agent Skills?'
